top_signals.title: US Stocks Pare Losses on Hormuz Headline Despite Yield Concerns
top_signals.summary: US stocks rebounded from earlier losses on a report that the US and Iran were discussing a phased deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, pulling oil down from the peak hit earlier in the session.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: S&P 500 Pares Its Decline on Hormuz Deal Hopes: Markets Wrap
top_signals.summary: Hopes for an agreement to revive energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz spurred a rebound in stocks from session lows, tempering worries about the impacts of still-elevated oil prices on inflation.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.

top_signals.title: Vitol Scoops Up 25 Million Barrels of Discounted Iraqi Crude
top_signals.summary: Vitol has bought at least 25 million barrels of Iraqi crude for September loading, making the world’s largest independent oil trader Iraq’s second-biggest buyer behind ADNOC as Baghdad pays steep discounts to keep barrels moving through the Strait of Hormuz. Iraq’s SOMO offered September crude at discounts of $15 to $20.80 per barrel to its official selling prices, according to a tender document reviewed by Reuters. Trading sources said some cargoes sold at even larger discounts. The discount buys something Iraq badly needs right…
